title: kbmon's sessions panel lists no process on Windows: bl_procs gives up because Windows exposes no working directory
goal: on Windows the sessions panel lists the clone's processes without a working directory: pid, parent, start and command name from the host's process table read through PowerShell (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process: ProcessId, ParentProcessId, Name, CommandLine as JSON), each with its checkout when a checkout path of the clone appears in its command line, beside the coord intents and the dispatch records' worker pids; the command line is only matched against checkout paths, never printed or kept; and in place of 'processes unreadable' the panel says plainly what Windows cannot show (a process whose command line names no checkout, so orphans told by working directory)

run:
import json,os,sys,tempfile,types
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools')
import mon_base,mon_sessions,bl_procs
root=os.path.realpath('.');d=tempfile.mkdtemp();me=os.getpid()
rows=[{'ProcessId':me,'ParentProcessId':os.getppid(),'Name':'claude.exe','CommandLine':'claude.exe --add-dir '+root}]
for n in ('powershell','pwsh','powershell.exe','pwsh.exe'):
    f=os.path.join(d,n);open(f,'w').write('#!/bin/sh\ncat <<"EOF"\n'+json.dumps(rows)+'\nEOF\n');os.chmod(f,0o755)
os.environ['PATH']=d+os.pathsep+os.environ.get('PATH','')
class Win(types.ModuleType):
    def __init__(s,real,**kw): super().__init__(real.__name__);s._r=real;s.__dict__.update(kw)
    def __getattr__(s,k): return getattr(s._r,k)
for m in (bl_procs,mon_sessions):
    m.os=Win(os,name='nt');m.sys=Win(sys,platform='win32')
data=mon_sessions.collect(mon_base.Ctx(root=mon_base.Path(root)))
text='\n'.join(mon_sessions.lines(data,200))
print(text[:600])
sys.exit(1 if 'processes unreadable' in text or str(me) not in text else 0)

notes: Operator feedback 2026-10-20, running kbmon on Windows: 'kbmon shows "processes unreadable: Windows does not expose a process working directory"'. Premise on origin/main 5970ced2c, 2026-10-20, simulated Windows (os.name nt and sys.platform win32 for bl_procs and mon_sessions only, since a global os.name breaks pathlib; a planted powershell/pwsh shim answering Win32_Process rows as JSON): the repro prints 'processes unreadable: Windows does not expose a process's working directory' and lists no pid. Cause: bl_procs.unsupported() returns that reason for os.name nt and cwd_map/snapshot return no processes at all, though worktrees and coord intents still show. The bl_procs rule 'a process's command line is never read' changes for Windows only: the command line is matched against checkout paths and dropped, never printed or kept. kb: Win32_Process has ParentProcessId and CommandLine [DOC S-hgt26zgs]; Get-CimInstance Win32_Process gives CommandLine, and the Learn example runs elevated, without which its query returns no results [DOC S-v6442u3l], so a non-elevated run may see no command line for another user's process: say so, never fail. Research ST-dtrqrwzo 2026-10-20: the kb holds no Microsoft statement that a non-elevated Win32_Process query returns CommandLine of another account's process; the gap entry (windows/process-parent-and-command-line) stays UNK, so the panel must treat a missing command line as a state and say so; a run on a Windows host, elevated and not, settles it.
